hints: Calculate speed at $t = 10\text{ s}$: $v = at = 3(10) = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the distance in the acceleration stage ($0 \le t \le 10$) using $s_1 = \frac{1}{2}(10)(30) = 150\text{ m}$.
Find the distance in the constant speed stage ($10 \le t \le 40$) using $s_2 = 30 \times 30 = 900\text{ m}$, then add the two distances.
walkthrough:
Calculate the speed of the car at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$v = at = 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the distance covered in the first $10\text{ s}$ and during the constant speed stage ($10$ to $40\text{ s}$):
$$s_1 = \frac{1}{2}(10)(30) = 150\text{ m}$$
$$s_2 = (40 - 10)(30) = 30 \times 30 = 900\text{ m}$$

Calculate total distance covered in the first $40\text{ s}$:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 150 + 900 = 1050\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The motion of the car during the first $40\text{ s}$ consists of two stages: uniform acceleration from rest for $10\text{ s}$, followed by constant speed for $30\text{ s}$.

Find the speed reached at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 3(10) = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

The distance in Stage 1 ($0$ to $10\text{ s}$) is the area of a triangle on the $v$-$t$ graph:
$$s_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 30 = 150\text{ m}$$

The distance in Stage 2 ($10$ to $40\text{ s}$) is the area of a rectangle of duration $\Delta t = 30\text{ s}$:
$$s_2 = 30 \times 30 = 900\text{ m}$$

Add the two distances together:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 150 + 900 = 1050\text{ m}$$

hints: The car covers the remaining $1500 - 1050 = 450\text{ m}$ while decelerating to rest from $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the car's deceleration time $t_{\text{dec}} = \frac{450}{15} = 30\text{ s}$, giving a total car time of $70\text{ s}$.
The motorcycle starts at $t = 20\text{ s}$ and stops at $t = 70\text{ s}$, so its total travel time is $50\text{ s}$.
Use the motorcycle's distance $1500 = \frac{1}{2}(30 + 50)V$ to find its maximum speed $V = 37.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
The remaining $20\text{ s}$ of motorcycle time splits into $5\text{ s}$ accelerating and $15\text{ s}$ decelerating, giving acceleration $a = \frac{37.5}{5} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Find the car's deceleration time over the remaining $450\text{ m}$:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{30 + 0}{2} t_{\text{dec}} = 15 t_{\text{dec}} = 450 \implies t_{\text{dec}} = 30\text{ s}$$

Find total time for the car and deduced travel time for the motorcycle:
$$t_{\text{car}} = 10 + 30 + 30 = 70\text{ s} \implies t_{\text{motorcycle}} = 70 - 20 = 50\text{ s}$$

Calculate the motorcycle's maximum speed $V$ using total distance $1500\text{ m}$:
$$1500 = \frac{1}{2}(30 + 50)V = 40V \implies V = \frac{1500}{40} = 37.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

With constant speed for $30\text{ s}$, the remaining $20\text{ s}$ splits into acceleration and deceleration:
$$a = \frac{V}{t_{\text{acc}}} = \frac{37.5}{5} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
First, determine the motion of the car in its deceleration phase. Total distance is $1500\text{ m}$, of which $1050\text{ m}$ was covered in the first $40\text{ s}$:
$$s_{\text{dec}} = 1500 - 1050 = 450\text{ m}$$

The car decelerates uniformly from $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 0$:
$$s_{\text{dec}} = \left(\frac{u + v}{2}\right)t_{\text{dec}} = \left(\frac{30 + 0}{2}\right)t_{\text{dec}} = 15t_{\text{dec}}$$
$$15t_{\text{dec}} = 450 \implies t_{\text{dec}} = 30\text{ s}$$
The car comes to rest at time $t = 10 + 30 + 30 = 70\text{ s}$.

The motorcycle starts at $t = 20\text{ s}$ and reaches the car at $t = 70\text{ s}$, giving a total journey time of:
$$t_{\text{motorcycle}} = 70 - 20 = 50\text{ s}$$

The motorcycle's $v$-$t$ graph is a trapezium with parallel sides of length $50\text{ s}$ (base) and $30\text{ s}$ (constant speed), with maximum speed $V$:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{30 + 50}{2} \times V = 40V$$
$$40V = 1500 \implies V = \frac{1500}{40} = 37.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

For $0 \le t \le 10$: accelerating from rest produces an increasing concave-up parabolic curve.
For $10 \le t \le 40$: constant speed produces a straight line with constant gradient $30$.

walkthrough:
Sketch the displacement-time graph passing through the four critical points:
$$(0,0), \quad (10, 150), \quad (40, 1050), \quad (70, 1500)$$
Stage 1 ($0 \le t \le 10$): Curve begins with zero gradient at the origin, increasing concave-up as the car accelerates uniformly.
Stage 2 ($10 \le t \le 40$): Straight line joining $(10, 150)$ to $(40, 1050)$ with constant positive gradient equal to $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Stage 3 ($40 \le t \le 70$): Increasing concave-down curve leveling off to a horizontal gradient (zero velocity) at $(70, 1500)$.

teacher_walkthrough: A displacement-time graph displays position as a function of time. Its gradient at any point represents instantaneous velocity.

Identify the key boundary points with coordinates $(t, s)$:
$$(0, 0), \quad (10, 150), \quad (40, 1050), \quad (70, 1500)$$
1. From $t = 0$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$: The car accelerates from rest. Gradient starts at zero and increases steadily. Draw a smooth concave-up parabolic curve from $(0,0)$ to $(10,150)$.
2. From $t = 10$ to $t = 40\text{ s}$: Speed is constant at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Draw a straight line connecting $(10,150)$ to $(40,1050)$ with constant slope $30$.

3. From $t = 40$ to $t = 70\text{ s}$: The car decelerates uniformly to rest. Velocity decreases to zero. Draw a concave-down curve from $(40,1050)$ to $(70,1500)$ with the tangent becoming completely horizontal at $t = 70\text{ s}$.
